questions.title: How do you establish operational practices for agentic AI systems?
questions.description: Agentic systems that are built on strong operational foundations (with clear roles, reliable handoffs, and tested failure recovery) earn stakeholder trust and scale confidently into production. These systems combine precedent and best practices from several architectural disciplines, including generative AI and multi-agent coordination. These practices can't be combined without careful consideration. They must be judiciously selected and refined based on the workload being built and the business problem being addressed. CODE REVIEW RESULT (2026-10-22, 01.A2A-multi-agent-incident-response): Expected risk: HIGH. Met: BP01. Partially met: -. Not met: BP02, BP03. Summary: Roles of Host (ADK), Monitoring (Strands) and WebSearch (OpenAI Agents) are clearly defined in system prompts, but there is no human escalation path and no failure-scenario testing.

questions.title: How do you manage prompt and configuration lifecycle?
questions.description: Agent prompts, configurations, and tool permissions define agent behavior and evolve continually as business needs change. Managing these artifacts requires balancing rapid iteration with stability so that changes are tracked, tested, and reversible. Summary: Prompts are hard-coded in prompt/__init__.py and can only change via a container rebuild. Model ID is managed as a CFN parameter. No drift detection or feedback loop.

choices.title: Evolve agent prompts, tool calls, and configurations to reflect evolving business needs

Improve: externalize prompt versions to Bedrock Prompt Management or SSM parameters. -- A prompt shapes agent behavior more directly than almost any other configuration artifact. Create a prompt lifecycle that applies code-grade discipline, versioning, review, evaluation, and rollback to prompts, which helps avoid unnoticed prompt drift and degraded decisions in agent interactions.

questions.title: How do you establish tool integration and management practices?
questions.description: Agents rely on external tools and services to complete work, and the way those integrations are managed determines whether agent behavior stays consistent as the tool inventory grows. Without a shared registry, standardized protocols, and common fallback behavior, every new tool adds operational burden and every tool failure risks broader agent outages. CODE REVIEW RESULT (2026-10-22, 01.A2A-multi-agent-incident-response): Expected risk: MEDIUM. Met: BP02. Partially met: BP01. Not met: BP03. Summary: CloudWatch tools are connected via AgentCore Gateway (MCP, Smithy model) and remote agents via A2A, both standard protocols. No fallback for tool errors.

choices.title: Implement tool registry and catalog management

helpfulResource.displayText: Review: Partially met: Gateway acts as the tool catalog (cloudformation/monitoring_agent.yaml:1444-1478, SearchType SEMANTIC). The Tavily tool (web_search_openai_agents/tools.py) is called directly outside the Gateway and is missing from the catalog. Improve: register Tavily as a Gateway target (OpenAPI) for a single catalog. -- Agents that can't discover tools end up with hardcoded integrations, inconsistent documentation, and a maintenance tax that grows with every new capability. A centralized registry makes the tool catalog queryable, versioned, and governable.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish standardized tool integration protocols (MCP, A2A)

questions.title: How do you secure agentic memory and securely manage state between agents?
questions.description: One reason agentic AI is effective is the ability to perform long-running tasks. To achieve a goal, agents need to store context, tasks, and results. Agent memory systems can be targeted to introduce false information or influence agent decisions, so securing memory and state helps maintain agent integrity. CODE REVIEW RESULT (2026-10-22, 01.A2A-multi-agent-incident-response): Expected risk: HIGH. Met: -. Partially met: -. Not met: BP01, BP02, BP03. Summary: (Top priority) Memory namespaces are designed as /technical-issues/(actorId) etc., but actorId is a header value set freely by the client, so spoofing it allows reading another user's long-term memory. Agent singletons are bound to the first request's actor/session, and memory content is injected into the system prompt without validation. No CMK.

choices.title: Implement memory isolation and integrity controls

helpfulResource.displayText: Review: Not met: in frontend/src/services/chatService.ts:40-46 the browser decodes the JWT and sets X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Custom-Actorid itself, host_adk_agent/main.py:31 trusts it without validation then spoofing another user's sub grants access to namespaces in monitoring_strands_agent/memory_hook.py:56-64 and web_search_openai_agents/memory_tool.py:71-76. Also the singletons in monitoring_strands_agent/agent_executor.py:33-52, web_search_openai_agents/agent_executor.py:34-36 and host_adk_agent/main.py:39-47 are bound to the first request's actor/session (implicitly relying on AgentCore per-session microVM isolation). AgentMemory has no EncryptionKeyArn. Improve: derive actorId server-side from the verified JWT sub claim (ignore the header or require a match), create/cache agents per (actor, session), apply a KMS CMK. -- Shared agent memory is the shortest path for a single affected session to contaminate every other one. Partitioning memory along the boundaries that matter for the workload, and verifying what comes back out, contains the scope of memory poisoning to the partition it touched.

questions.title: How do you control and secure agent tool usage?
questions.description: Agents interact with external systems through tools such as APIs, databases, file systems, and other services. Without proper controls, an agent with tool access can be directed to perform unintended actions. Authorization, input validation, and tool governance reduce the risk of tool misuse and unauthorized operations. CODE REVIEW RESULT (2026-10-22, 01.A2A-multi-agent-incident-response): Expected risk: HIGH. Met: -. Partially met: BP01, BP03. Not met: BP02.
